claim: Framer documents production-adjacent MCP design workflows with branch review
verifiedFacts: Framer published an October 30 article documenting its team's use of Framer MCP for website edits, migrations, search-informed copy changes, and CMS drafts.
Its examples explicitly keep human review and branch previews between agent edits and publication.
The article describes internal workflows, not independent measurements of commercial customer outcomes.
inference: An agent-assisted site repair and provenance service can sell reviewable changes and QA evidence rather than generic AI site generation.
Melodyfire and LithoMemphis should retain distinct design systems while sharing a bounded handoff and review protocol.
Advisory client problem: Clients need traceable website changes that preserve editable layers, branding, and approval.
Project disposition recommendation only: MelodicBloom/melodyfire, MelodicBloom/lithomemphis, MelodicBloom/kozo-dreams; no implementation executed.
significance: A design-tool provider publicly documents branch-based, human-reviewed agent editing as an operational pattern relevant to consultancy delivery.
assumptions: Framer MCP workflows can be reproduced on client projects with appropriate permissions.
knownLimitations: Examples are vendor-selected and do not measure defect rates, time savings, or customer demand.
No Framer project was connected or edited.
